doc.title: Junior Mance Part I interviewed by Monk Rowe and Michael Woods, New York City, New York, July 27, 1995 [interview 1 of 2]

title: Mistakes in jazz: Miles, Oscar Peterson and Bird's Lover Man
summary: Miles on Oscar Peterson, Bird's Lover Man, and live recording at Capitol.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Exactly. Yeah. Because you know, it’s funny, Miles Davis made the statement once he says, “Man I don’t like Oscar Peterson.” I say, “Why?” He says, “Because he never makes a mistake.” Which Oscar doesn’t. Oscar is flawless when he plays all the time. But Miles, you know Miles made a lot of mistakes, so did Bird. But to us, we figure it was supposed to be like that. It’s like Steve Martin when he stumbles and falls, oh I meant to do that. Like you remember, there’s a record that’s really a classic, one Bird made, “Lover Man.” You know this is when he was, right after that they carted him off to Camarillo, because he was losing it you know? This record sounds so great. I mean the feeling was there. He made a lot of mistakes, but he covered them up. They don’t sound like mistakes. And that solo turned out to be a classic. They had more young musicians imitating that solo.
Some people even will say that you come up with your best ideas when you paint yourself into a corner.
You say how am I gonna get out of this, you know.
